# Cleaner Reference

This document describes each cleaner available in CleanMac.

## System Cleaners

### system-cache

**Description**: Cleans user application caches

**Paths cleaned**:
- `~/Library/Caches/*`

**Risk level**: Low

**Notes**: Caches are automatically regenerated by applications. Cleaning may cause temporary slowdowns as apps rebuild their caches.

---

### system-logs

**Description**: Cleans user application logs

**Paths cleaned**:
- `~/Library/Logs/*`

**Risk level**: Low

**Notes**: Old logs are generally safe to remove. Consider keeping recent logs for debugging.

---

### trash

**Description**: Empties the user's trash

**Paths cleaned**:
- `~/.Trash/*`

**Risk level**: Low

**Configuration options**:
- `min_age_days`: Only clean items older than this

**Notes**: Unlike other cleaners, this actually deletes files since they're already in trash.

---

## Developer Cleaners

### xcode

**Description**: Cleans Xcode build artifacts

**Paths cleaned**:
- `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/*`
- `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/Archives/*`
- `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/iOS DeviceSupport/*`
- `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/watchOS DeviceSupport/*`
- `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/tvOS DeviceSupport/*`

**Risk level**: Medium (Archives)

**Configuration options**:
- `keep_recent_archives_days`: Keep archives newer than this
- `keep_ios_versions`: Array of iOS versions to keep

**Notes**: DerivedData can be large and is safe to remove. Archives may be needed for app distribution.

---

### homebrew

**Description**: Cleans Homebrew cache and old versions

**Paths cleaned**:
- `/opt/homebrew/` (Apple Silicon)
- `/usr/local/` (Intel)

**Risk level**: Low

**Configuration options**:
- `keep_versions`: Number of old versions to keep

**Notes**: Uses `brew cleanup` internally.

---

### npm

**Description**: Cleans npm package cache

**Paths cleaned**:
- `~/.npm/_cacache/*`

**Risk level**: Low

**Notes**: Safe to remove; packages will be re-downloaded when needed.

---

### yarn

**Description**: Cleans Yarn package cache

**Paths cleaned**:
- `~/.yarn/cache/*`
- `~/Library/Caches/Yarn/*`

**Risk level**: Low

**Notes**: Safe to remove; packages will be re-downloaded when needed.

---

### cargo

**Description**: Cleans Rust/Cargo package cache

**Paths cleaned**:
- `~/.cargo/registry/cache/*`
- `~/.cargo/registry/src/*`

**Risk level**: Low

**Configuration options**:
- `keep_recent_days`: Keep crates used recently

**Notes**: Safe to remove; crates will be re-downloaded when needed.

---

### pip

**Description**: Cleans Python pip cache

**Paths cleaned**:
- `~/Library/Caches/pip/*`
- `~/.cache/pip/*`

**Risk level**: Low

**Notes**: Safe to remove; packages will be re-downloaded when needed.

---

### docker

**Description**: Cleans Docker images, volumes, and build cache

**Risk level**: Medium to High

**Configuration options**:
- `dangling_only`: Only clean dangling images (safer)
- `clean_volumes`: Clean unused volumes (CAUTION!)
- `clean_build_cache`: Clean build cache

**Notes**:
- Volumes may contain important data!
- Uses `docker system prune` and related commands

---

## App Cleaners

### apps

**Description**: Finds leftover files from uninstalled applications

**Paths searched**:
- `~/Library/Application Support/`
- `~/Library/Preferences/`
- `~/Library/Caches/`
- `~/Library/Logs/`
- `~/Library/Containers/`
- `~/Library/Group Containers/`
- `~/Library/Saved Application State/`

**Risk level**: High

**Configuration options**:
- `known_apps`: Array of bundle IDs for known uninstalled apps

**Notes**:
- Requires `--force` flag
- Only cleans explicitly listed bundle IDs
- Review carefully before cleaning
